page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-192 is a high-density, compute-focused server instance powered by 5th Gen Intel Xeon 8581C processors operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Built on an x86_64 architecture with 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated execution threads, the instance incorporates a multi-level cache topology featuring 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache array. It is provisioned with 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes neither bundled local NVMe storage nor discrete GPUs.

The Emerald Rapids microarchitecture integrates specialized instructions including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) alongside AVX-512 vector pipelines and hardware cryptographic engines. In multi-threaded evaluations, the configuration demonstrates top-tier compute performance, recording a multi-core stress-ng result of 165,322.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,306.0. Memory subsystems deliver 597.08 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 255.61 GB/sec in write operations. Software compilation workloads utilizing Clang reached a top-tier score of 59,793.0, complemented by 966.77 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Hardware-level AMX acceleration translates into high CPU-based inference capability, recording 302.56 prompt tokens per second and 47.25 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Network and caching efficiency is reflected in 225.8 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 208.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Because local persistent disks are omitted, all stateful persistence depends on external network storage. This resource balance is tailored for parallel compute workloads, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, CPU matrix operations, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-192 is a compute-focused instance featuring 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with a dedicated CPU allocation, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 384.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), the server is engineered for high-concurrency CPU workloads. The instance does not include integrated local storage or discrete GPUs. Equipped with Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, it achieves top-tier multi-threaded benchmark results, including 165,322.49 in stress-ng multi-core and 21,306.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth attains 597.08 GB/sec for large-block reads, alongside strong LLM inference throughput on medium and large parameter models. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents an efficient density tradeoff for compute-bound operations, making this configuration well matched for distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, Redis caching nodes, and parallel numerical simulation tasks.
